chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Sayf ibn 'Amirah, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, who said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about a man who bought a pregnant slave girl, and her pregnancy had become evident, so he slept with her. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Evil is what he has done.' I said: 'So what do you say regarding it?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Did he isolate (withdraw) from her or not?' I said: 'Answer me regarding the two aspects.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'If he had isolated from her, let him fear Allah and not repeat (the act), and if he had not isolated from her, he should not sell that child, nor inherit him, but he should emancipate him and allocate for him something from his wealth by which he can live, for he has nourished him with his seed.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a child born to a slave girl purchased by her owner after he slept with her?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the Shia jurisprudence of 'Iqat' (emancipation) for the offspring of a slave woman whose owner consummates relations with her, distinguishing between pre-existing and newly conceived pregnancy. It establishes that the child is not merely inherited but freed and supported from the owner's estate, reflecting the principle that the father's seed provides a form of nourishment justifying continued care. This ruling underscores the ethical obligation of the master to ensure the slave's child achieves freedom and financial stability, a key concept in Shia family law.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Say Bin Ameyra, from Is’haq Bin Ammar who said,

‘I asked Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> about a man who bought a pregnant slave girl and her pregnancy had manifested, so he slept with her. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Evil is what he has done’. I said, ‘So what are you<sup>asws</sup> saying regarding it?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Is he isolated from her or not?’ I said, ‘Answer me regarding the two aspects’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If he had isolated, so let him fear Allah<sup>azwj</sup> and he should not repeat, and if he had not isolated from her, so she should not sell that child, and he would not inherit him, but he should emancipate him and make something from his wealth to be for him he can live by, for he had nourished him with his seed’.
